reviewPosture: This review owes the artifact nothing. Every figure it publishes was recomputed from bytes on disk rather than read from the artifact, per IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.2.2: measurements get hard comparison, invariants get semantic gates. Where the artifact binds anything as a derivation over its predecessor, the derivation was RESOLVED and the resolved result compared against the stated result, per section 7.3 and the CMP-IR-01 record. Four blocking findings are reported. Three of the four were found by resolving rather than by reading.

verdict.overall: REJECT FOR REPAIR -- 4 blocking findings, 9 non-blocking observations
verdict.sealRecommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL (unchanged; not this review's to change)
verdict.statusChangesMadeByThisReview: NONE. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. durableDefault remains UNSELECTED in the binding packet. No artifact was signed, sealed, applied, frozen or restatused. This review wrote exactly one file: itself. retention-tiers.v25.json was not edited, and its digest is byte-identical at the end of this review to the digest at dispatch.
verdict.whyRejectRatherThanAcceptWithObservation: Three separate blockers are cases where the artifact's stated conclusion and its stated mechanism disagree, and in each case the mechanism -- which is what an implementer builds from -- is the wrong one. B1 is the sharpest: the artifact spends an entire section, a proof, three negative controls and a departure record attacking a shipping-product defect in which a bound's disable behaviour sits outside the bound's expression, and then publishes three demand expressions whose disable behaviour sits outside the expression, each of which evaluates to 'evict the entire evictable set' at its own declared disable value -- which is the DEFAULT configuration of every unconfigured project. The direction of that failure is toward more deletion, which is the direction this artifact itself names as the worst possible one for a silent failure.
verdict.whatIsGoodAndShouldSurviveTheRepair: The central design judgement -- a total resolution rule rather than a schema field, with provenance carried alongside posture and the default never persisted -- is correct, well argued, and survives every attack this review made on it. The EPHEMERAL_ONLY-IS-ALWAYS-CONSENTED property holds on the resolved decision table. The refusal genuinely moves rather than vanishing. The artifact's authority hygiene is the best in this lineage: it designs against an unapplied draft without once leaning on it as authority, and it reports the measurement over the expectation in the one place where the draft asserted a closure that the live D9 bytes refute. None of the four blockers touches the posture design itself.

There is no operation list -- no set/add verbs, no paths, no values -- so check-completeness.py's derivation reader, which locates a derivation by shape as one artifact filename plus one sha256 plus one non-empty operation list, would not recognise this as a derivation at all. blockers.severity: BLOCKING -- the strongest finding of this review
blockers.statement: The three published demand expressions do not encode their own disable semantics. Each one, evaluated at the value the artifact declares disables it, returns len(evictable) -- evict the entire evictable set -- rather than 0. The disable behaviour lives in a sibling scalar, disabledWhen, outside every expression. Since the defaulted bounds are 0 / 0 / 0, this is the configuration of every project that has never been configured.

publishedExpressions.size: the smallest k such that total_bytes(evictable[k:]) <= maxTotalBytes, or len(evictable) if no such k exists, disabledWhen maxTotalBytes == 0
publishedExpressions.time: the number of leading members of the eviction order whose admission time is older than now - maxAgeSeconds, disabledWhen maxAgeSeconds == 0

evaluatedAtTheDefault.demand_time_at_maxAgeSeconds_0: every member already admitted, since 'older than now - 0' is 'older than now'; 5
evaluatedAtTheDefault.meaning: the entire evictable set is purged

whatTheArtifactAssertsInstead: $.partC_retentionBounds.sweep.neverRunsWhenBoundsAreDefaulted.statement: 'with provenance DEFAULTED the three values are 0, every demand is 0, and the sweep emits nothing'
$.partC_retentionBounds.sweep.boundIndependence.proof: 'Disabling a bound sets its demand to 0'
measured.underTheGuardedReading: applying disabledWhen as a guard outside each expression, all 5 rows agree exactly, including every expectedCauses value. So the artifact's INTENT is unambiguous and correct. Its published MECHANISM is not the intent.

whyThisIsBlockingAndNotCosmetic: The failure direction is toward MORE deletion, on the default configuration, in every project nobody has configured. $.shippingProductEvidence.departed[1].why names that exact direction as 'the worst possible direction for a silent failure'.

The time dimension is the worst of the three, and it is the one DEP-RT25-01 forces to 0. maxAgeSeconds MUST be 0 until that dependency resolves -- and 0 is precisely the value at which the published time expression demands the whole set. So the only legal configuration of the age bound is the one whose published expression evicts everything.

It is the same shape the artifact is written to refuse, one level up. $.partC_retentionBounds.sweep.boundIndependence.theDefectThisRefusesToInherit says of the shipping product: 'The defect is not that one guard sits in the wrong place. It is that the size demand was expressed in terms of the count configuration at all... Making each demand a pure function of its own configured value and the shared order makes the class unrepresentable.' The artifact then makes each demand a pure function whose value at its own disable point is wrong, and reintroduces an out-of-expression guard to correct it. The guard is a different guard in a different place; it is still a guard outside the expression.

boundIndependence.proof is not a proof of what the expressions do. 'Disabling a bound sets its demand to 0' is asserted, not derived from the published expressions, and is false of them. The monotonicity argument that follows is correct about max and irrelevant to the defect.
blockers.whatRepairWouldLookLike: State each demand as a total expression that is correct at every value in its domain, for example demand_count := 0 if keepCount == 0 else max(0, len(evictable) - keepCount), and the same for the other two -- so that the disable behaviour is inside the function rather than beside it. Then the boundIndependence proof becomes a statement about the published expressions rather than about an unstated guarded version of them, and PC-V-01 through PC-V-04 become checks on what is published.
blockers.confidence: VERY HIGH. Reproduced by direct evaluation of the published expressions against the artifact's own five arithmetic rows. The contradiction is internal and needs no external premise.

blockers.statement: The artifact declares one rule as the generator of the entire Part A repair, marks it derivedNotEnumerated true, and names exactly two exceptions to it. Resolved against v24's own cells, the rule needs at least two more exceptions, and applied literally it produces a Part A that is materially worse than the one the artifact describes -- it deletes the first-run disclosure from every ABSENT cell and deletes the only ask in the table.
blockers.theRuleVerbatim: every ABSENT row now behaves exactly as the corresponding PRESENT-DURABLE_RETAINED row, except that no policy is persisted and the provenance is DEFAULTED

measured.method: For each of the four (invocationProfile, requestedCustody) pairs, diff v24's ABSENT cell against v24's PRESENT-DURABLE_RETAINED cell field by field. Every field on which they differ is a field the rule silently changes.
unstatedExceptionsRequired: firstRunDisclosureEmitted must NOT follow the rule. All four ABSENT cells carry true and all four PRESENT-DURABLE_RETAINED cells carry false. Applied literally the rule sets all four to false, deleting the first-run disclosure from exactly the cells that exist to carry it. The artifact lists $.partA_firstRunRetentionConsent.disclosure among surfaces it does not change, so the intent is plainly that the disclosure survives -- but the rule as written removes it.

askPerformed must NOT follow the rule at local-interactive / DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE. v24 index 7 carries true and v24 index 11 carries false. Applied literally the rule sets index 7's askPerformed to false, taking askPerformedCellCount from 1 to 0 -- while the artifact states askPerformedCellCountAfter 1, askStillPerformed true, and builds a whole paragraph (whyTheAskSurvives) on the ask surviving.

whyThisIsBlockingAndNotCosmetic: The ask is not decorative. It is the ONLY path by which provenance can ever become CONSENTED. $.overriddenArchitecturalRecommendation.whatMitigatesThem[0] names it as the first mitigation of the override's named exposure: 'The ask still happens at the first local-interactive durable-authoritative run, so the un-asked window is bounded by the first interactive use rather than lasting forever.' An implementer who applies the artifact's own stated generator deletes that mitigation and makes CONSENTED unreachable from a fresh project by any path. DEP-RT25-07's whatWouldChangeIfItWereRevisited says 'only the CI cell. The local-interactive cell reaches an ask on the first durable run' -- which is false of the artifact's own generating rule.

The first-run disclosure is the other half. Deleting firstRunDisclosureEmitted from the ABSENT cells means durable evidence is written into a user's project with neither an ask nor a disclosure, which is strictly worse than the exposure the product authority was told about and accepted.

derivedNotEnumerated true is an explicit instruction to derive rather than to read the enumeration, so the rule is the normative artefact and the two changed cells are illustrations of it. The artifact says so: 'those are enumerable BY MEASUREMENT rather than by search'. The measurement was not run over all fields, only over outcomes.
Section 7.3 and CMP-IR-01 are the governing rule: a derivation must be resolved, not read. Resolved, this one does not produce what the artifact says it produces.
blockers.whatTheArtifactAlreadyHalfKnows: RT25-RES-05 concedes that no instrument confirmed the 2 cells and 4 outcomes are ALL the places that branch on absence. That is the right residual for the wrong axis: the gap is not only which SITES were found, it is which FIELDS the generating rule touches at the sites that were found.
blockers.whatRepairWouldLookLike: Either state the rule with its full exception set -- posture-derived behaviour follows PRESENT-DURABLE_RETAINED, while firstRunDisclosureEmitted, askPerformed and policy persistence do not -- or drop derivedNotEnumerated and publish the two changed cells as complete field-by-field rows, which is what an implementer needs anyway and what v24 does.

dispositionOfRT25RES02.theArtifactsOwnInvitation: $.partC_retentionBounds.section46DischargePreservation.saidLoudlyAsRequired states: 'A reviewer who disagrees with the structural argument should treat this as a blocker rather than an observation.' This review takes the invitation seriously and answers it explicitly rather than by silence.
dispositionOfRT25RES02.theArgumentUnderTest: That closing the cause partition cannot disturb P5-CAUSE-BLIND, because the fold rule states the current state of a raw key is the toState of its last entry, the algorithm reads no other field of a ledger entry, and cause is therefore already unreachable from the derivation.
dispositionOfRT25RES02.adjudication: THE ARGUMENT IS ACCEPTED. RT25-RES-02 is NOT escalated to a blocker.
reasoning: The premise is checkable without an instrument and this reviewer checked it: v24's effectiveCapabilityDerivation declares exactly three inputs, none of which is a ledger entry field other than through the fold, and its algorithm and foldRule read toState only. The 11-member forbiddenInputs list contains no field of an entry at all.

The change is monotone in the safe direction. Adding cause to forbiddenInputs takes the list from 11 to 12 and can only shrink the set of inputs the function may read. It cannot admit an input previously refused, so it cannot weaken P1 through P5.

RT25-C-INV-05 is genuinely strictly stronger than P5, not a restatement: P5 is blindness ACROSS states, RT25-C-INV-05 is blindness WITHIN a state. Strengthening a property whose mechanism you have not changed does not require re-running the trials that established the weaker one.

The artifact itself identifies this as the riskiest part of the change, names why, and declines to claim the 40,000 trials travel to these bytes. whatIsNotClaimed is four items long and all four are correct disclaimers.
dispositionOfRT25RES02.theBoundOnThatAcceptance: This is acceptance of an ARGUMENT, not verification of a PROPERTY. Section 7.8's standing bound applies: what discharges a residual is independent re-derivation, not more assertions from the same lane. This reviewer re-read the predecessor's algorithm and confirmed the premise; it did not re-run the 46 cause comparisons with the partition populated, and no instrument exists that could. RT25-RES-02 stands as written and its howItWouldClose is the right closing condition.

Three of v25's claims about that input therefore could not be checked at all: the two staleness observations and the quoted 'closes residual RT23-B-RES-01' phrase. Everything in $.shippingProductEvidence. This reviewer did not open /Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/opensip-cli and re-measured none of the 7 recorded product claims. The predecessor reviews' from-scratch derivations: the 40,000 randomised trials, the 276 exhaustive derivations, the 46 cause comparisons and the two sealed unitId recomputations. None was re-run. v25 does not claim them and explicitly disclaims their travel, so nothing in this verdict rests on them.

That v24 and v23 are correct within themselves. This review compared v25 against their bytes; it did not re-adjudicate them. IR-RT25-N06 records one internal inconsistency in v24 found incidentally and escalates nothing.
The correctness of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md's own text as an authority. It was read as data and quoted from, not audited.

This is RT25-RES-05's own declared gap and this review did not close it: no mechanical walk of v24's Part A for presence tests was performed. Whether accepting the posture decision is WISE. That is a product judgement and no oracle exists for it. This review adjudicated whether the artifact designs against it honestly and mechanically correctly, and on the first count the answer is emphatically yes.

Mutation resistance of any kind. No leaf was respelled as a float, a boolean or a numeric string and re-admitted, because no instrument exists to admit it. RT25-RES-CORPUS-02 states this about the artifact's own census and it is equally true of this review.
